A0234.title: Embodied Data-Collection Privacy Protection
A0234.definition: Protecting privacy data collected by robot-mounted cameras/microphones in homes, malls, and factories via on-device processing, data desensitization, collection notice and consent, and differential privacy.
A0234.description:
Embodied data-collection privacy protection addresses incidents like iRobot Roomba J7 private-image leakage, Ecovacs remote eavesdropping, and Amazon Astro home surveillance, building protection across the data lifecycle. First, on-device processing — sensitive data (faces, voiceprints, home layout) is inferred locally on the robot, not uploaded to the cloud. Second, data desensitization — training/annotation data that must be uploaded is face-blurred, voice-pitched, and layout-generalized. Third, collection notice and consent — robots explicitly notify users of collection scope and purpose before collection, obtaining explicit consent. Fourth, differential privacy — noise is added to statistical data to prevent reverse-engineering individuals from aggregates.

This measure works with A0069 (privacy-enhancing technologies) and A0078 (endpoint detection and response), specialized for the physical-world collection scenario of embodied devices, core to GDPR and Personal Information Protection Law compliance for embodied intelligence.
A0234.limitation: On-device processing is limited by device compute, making complex models hard to deploy locally; desensitization may lose training-data value, affecting model performance; notice-and-consent can be perfunctory, with users hard-pressed to truly understand collection consequences; differential privacy significantly reduces data utility in low-cardinality scenarios.
